label: Zambia: South Luangwa, 13 nights · Jan 12
title: Zambia: South Luangwa in the green season
summary: 13 nights at Mfuwe in South Luangwa: afternoon drives that run into night drives every day (leopards, lions, hyenas), morning drives on 5 days, hippos and elephants on the Luangwa River. Budget tented camp, drives paid per drive. ~$5,505 pp.
overview:
- **What this is:** almost the whole trip in one of Africa's best parks for big cats, in the green season. **South Luangwa** has a lot of leopards, and its afternoon drives run on after dark with a spotlight. Lions are common, and the Luangwa River is packed with hippos and crocodiles. Elephants walk through the Mfuwe camps.
- **Dates:** LAX Sat Dec 26 → LAX Tue Jan 12. 15 nights on the ground: 2 in Lusaka, **13 in South Luangwa**, plus 2 on planes.
- **Route:** Lusaka 1n → ✈ Mfuwe → **South Luangwa 13n** (Croc Valley Camp at the Mfuwe gate) → ✈ Lusaka 1n → home.
- **Green season:** the bush is green, impala and puku have young (so the cats are busy), and the park is nearly empty. Many camps deep inside the park close; the Mfuwe-gate camps stay open, and the main loops near the Mfuwe bridge stay drivable. Expect afternoon storms and the odd cancelled drive. Thirteen nights gives plenty of slack.
- **Drives:** an afternoon drive every day that turns into a night drive (leopard, lion, hyena, genet, civet, porcupine, owls), and morning drives on 5 days. That's 18 drives, about $60 each plus $25 a day in park fees. Rest mornings in camp are for the elephants and hippos at the river and for the heat.
- **Herps:** the rains are the best time: flap-necked chameleons in the spotlight, bullfrogs, monitors, crocodiles, pythons and puff adders crossing the roads at night.
- **No Lake Malawi:** dropped in favour of safari days. Malawi is in a fuel crisis (Oct 2026) and Americans need a visa again. Two lake nights stay as an option.
- **Budget: ~$5,505 pp** (≈ $11,010 for two). The ~$500 over $5k is the price of 13 nights. Cut 3 Luangwa nights (−$600) or fly in via Lilongwe (−$250) to get under it.

itinerary.title: Fly toward Lusaka
itinerary.details: Ethiopian via Addis Ababa, or Qatar via Doha or Emirates via Dubai, ~28–32h with connections. Pick a routing that lands in Lusaka by Dec 27 evening.

itinerary.title: Land in Lusaka
itinerary.details: Visa-free entry for US citizens (confirm before you fly). Change some dollars to kwacha, buy an Airtel or MTN SIM, and stay at a guesthouse near the airport. Lusaka is UTC+2.

itinerary.title: Fly to Mfuwe, first night drive
itinerary.details: Morning Proflight to Mfuwe (~1h15). The camp transfer takes ~40 min to Croc Valley on the Luangwa River, just outside the Mfuwe gate. Hippos grunting in front of camp. 16:00 drive into the park: puku, impala, Thornicroft's giraffe, then a spotlight on the way back after dark for leopard, genets and hyena.

itinerary.title: Rest morning, river and night drive
itinerary.details: Sleep off the travel. The camp sits on the river: hippos, crocodiles, elephants walking through camp, vervets and baboons. Afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: First morning drive
itinerary.details: 06:00 morning drive, the best time for lions on a kill and for wild dog, which are possible in the green season. Back by 10:00 before the heat. Afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: Night drive, New Year's Eve in camp
itinerary.details: Rest morning. Afternoon and night drive, then New Year's Eve at the camp bar over the river.

itinerary.title: Morning and night drives
itinerary.details: Morning drive and afternoon/night drive. Ask the guide to work the lagoons and oxbows (Wamilombe, Mfuwe lagoon) for big hippo pods, crocodiles and wading birds.

itinerary.title: Rest morning, night drive
itinerary.details: Morning in camp or a walk to the Tribal Textiles workshop nearby. Afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: Night drive for leopard
itinerary.details: Rest morning. Afternoon and night drive, concentrating on the leopard areas the guides have been tracking this week.

itinerary.title: Morning and night drives
itinerary.details: Morning drive and afternoon/night drive. Bring a headtorch for the camp paths: frogs, geckos and the occasional snake after rain.

itinerary.title: Rest morning, night drive
itinerary.details: Rest morning; laundry. Afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: Night drive
itinerary.details: Rest morning. Afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: Rest morning, night drive
itinerary.details: Rest morning. Afternoon and night drive. If a drive was rained off earlier in the week, add a morning drive here.

itinerary.title: Last night drive
itinerary.details: Rest morning. Last afternoon and night drive.

itinerary.title: Last morning drive, fly to Lusaka
itinerary.details: Last morning drive, brunch, then the transfer to Mfuwe airport and the afternoon Proflight to Lusaka. Night near the airport, as a buffer for Proflight schedule changes.

itinerary.title: Fly home
itinerary.details: International departure via Addis, Doha or Dubai.

alternatives.name: Fly into Lilongwe and drive to Mfuwe
alternatives.description: Lilongwe is ~4.5–5h by road from Mfuwe (via Chipata), and camps run transfers. Replaces the Proflight tickets and Lusaka nights with a road transfer (~$300 per vehicle each way). Needs a Malawi visa ($50), and Malawi's fuel shortage makes the Malawi leg less certain.

alternatives.description: Mukambi Safari Lodge is the one camp in central Kafue that stays open in the rains: a different, wilder park with leopard and lion, ~4h by road from Lusaka. ~$380 pp/night full board plus the road transfer.

practical:
## Entry
- **Zambia:** visa-free for US citizens per 2026 sources (30–90 days; the sources disagree). Passport valid 6+ months with 2 blank pages; carry proof of the onward flight.
- **Yellow fever:** not required arriving from the US; transiting Addis for under 12h doesn't trigger it.

## Packing
- Warm layer for night drives (open vehicles, wind after rain); rain jacket.
- Headtorch each; the camp paths have hippos and elephants at night, so always walk with a guard after dark.
- Binoculars; a fast lens for spotlight work (no flash at animals).
- Neutral colours; insect repellent with DEET; tsetse flies are around, and dark blue and black attract them.

## Money
- US dollars are accepted at the camp; **park fees in cash** (no cards at the gate). Kwacha for small purchases; ATMs in Lusaka and Mfuwe.

## Season
- Late December to January is the wet season: hot (~30–35 °C), humid, heavy afternoon storms. Some interior roads close; the Mfuwe sector loops stay open. Proflight sometimes shifts times in the rains; that's why the plan has a Lusaka night at both ends.

## Health and safety
- Check travel.state.gov for Zambia before booking. The main safety rule here is wildlife: hippos and elephants walk through the Mfuwe camps.
- Malaria is high-risk in the rains: prophylaxis plus long sleeves and repellent at dusk.
- The nearest good hospital is in Lusaka or Johannesburg; evacuation cover is essential.
